q: the son[3] of Philyra gave to him of exceeding might, even to the son of Peleas, when he had lost his sire: first that of all gods he most reverence Kronos' son, the deep-voiced lord of lightnings and of thunders, and then that he never rob of like honour a parent's spell of life.

s: Zeus is a Kronos' son (deep-voiced lord of lightnings and thunders)
q: first that of all gods he most reverence Kronos' son, the deep-voiced lord of lightnings and of thunders

s: Antilochos exemplifies parental honor and duty (by dying for his father)
q: Also of old time had mighty Antilochos this mind within him, who died for his father's sake, when he abode the murderous onset of Memnon, the leader of the Ethiop hosts.

s: Xenokrates of Akragas wins chariot-race victory
q: FOR XENOKRATES OF AKRAGAS, WINNER IN THE CHARIOT-RACE.

s: Antilochos's death for his father is an example of parental honor and duty (in the ancient heroic age)
q: So by the young men of that ancient time he was deemed to have wrought a mighty deed, and in succouring of parents to be supreme.

s: Antilochos dies for Nestor (his father)
q: For Nestor's chariot was stayed by a horse that was stricken of the arrows of Paris, and Memnon made at him with his mighty spear. Then the heart of the old man of Messene was troubled, and he cried unto his son; nor wasted he his words in vain; in his place stood up the godlike man and bought his father's flight by his own death.

s: Memnon leads the Ethiop hosts
q: Memnon, the leader of the Ethiop hosts.

s: Thrasyboulos handles wealth (with wisdom and without unrighteous or overweening youth)
q: And following his uncle also he hath made glory to appear for him; and with wisdom doth he handle wealth, neither gathereth the fruit of an unrighteous or overweening youth, but rather of knowledge amid the secret places of the Pierides.

s: Thrasyboulos honors Poseidon (as Earthshaker, by drawing near with glad heart)
q: And to thee, Earthshaker, who didst devise ventures of steeds, with right glad heart he draweth nigh.

s: Thrasyboulos has hospitality (a spirit sweeter than the honeycomb toward his guests)
q: Sweet is his spirit toward the company of his guests, yea sweeter than the honeycomb, the toil of bees.

s: chariot-race victory is in chariot-race
q: FOR XENOKRATES OF AKRAGAS, WINNER IN THE CHARIOT-RACE.

s: Pindar is age twenty-eight years (when the victory was won)
q: This victory was won B.C. 494, when Pindar was twenty-eight years old,

s: Xenokrates of Akragas is a son (of Ainesidamos)
q: Xenokrates was a son of Ainesidamos and brother of Theron.

s: Xenokrates of Akragas is a brother (of Theron)
q: Xenokrates was a son of Ainesidamos and brother of Theron.

s: Akragas is by riverside
q: For there for the blissful Emmenidai, and for Akragas by the riverside, and chiefliest for Xenokrates, is builded a ready treasure of song within the valley of Apollo rich in golden gifts.

s: the Emmenidai are beneficiaries of song (a ready treasure built within Apollo's valley)
q: For there for the blissful Emmenidai, and for Akragas by the riverside, and chiefliest for Xenokrates, is builded a ready treasure of song within the valley of Apollo rich in golden gifts.

q: For there for the blissful Emmenidai, and for Akragas by the riverside, and chiefliest for Xenokrates, is builded a ready treasure of song within the valley of Apollo rich in golden gifts.

s: Megakles is a member of the Alkmaionidai
q: He was a member of the great house of the Alkmaionidai

s: Alkmaionidai rebuilds Apollo's temple (with large sums; lately)
q: The Alkmainodai had lately been spending large sums on the rebuilding of Apollo's temple at Delphi.

s: Megakles wins victories at Isthmos (five)
q: And I hereto am led by victories, at Isthmos five

s: Megakles wins victory at Olympia (one, at the feast of Zeus)
q: and one pre-eminent, won at Olympia at the feast of Zeus

s: Megakles wins victories at Kirrha (two)
q: and two at Kirrha, which thou, O Megakles, and thy sire have won.

s: Megakles is ostracized twice
q: Megakles was twice ostracized.

s: four-horse chariot-race has winner winner (in the four-horse chariot-race)
q: WINNER IN THE FOUR-HORSE CHARIOT-RACE.

s: Megakles wins four-horse chariot-race
q: WINNER IN THE FOUR-HORSE CHARIOT-RACE.

s: Megakles's victory occurs in 490 B.C.
q: Megakles won this victory B.C. 490, the year of the battle of Marathon.

s: Megakles is probably nephew of Kleisthenes (possibly the son of Kleisthenes)
q: this Megakles was probably the nephew, possibly the son, of Kleisthenes.

s: Alkmaionidai includes Megakles
q: He was a member of the great house of the Alkmaionidai

s: Kleisthenes belongs to Alkmaionidai
q: He was a member of the great house of the Alkmaionidai, to which Kleisthenes and Perikles belonged.

s: Perikles belongs to Alkmaionidai
q: He was a member of the great house of the Alkmaionidai, to which Kleisthenes and Perikles belonged.

s: Aristomenes is a winner (in the wrestling-match at the Pythian games)
q: welcome thou this honour to Aristomenes, won in the Pythian games.

s: Peace is a daughter (daughter of Righteousness)
q: O kindly Peace, daughter of Righteousness

s: Peace makes great cities (through her power)
q: thou that makest cities great

s: Peace holds keys (the supreme keys of counsels and of wars)
q: and boldest the supreme keys of counsels and of wars

s: Peace sinks Insolence (in the sea when moved to relentless wrath)
q: and sinkest Insolence in the sea.

s: Righteousness is a daughter (mother of Peace)
q: O kindly Peace, daughter of Righteousness

s: Righteousness stands by song of triumph (as a companion to the poet's song)
q: By the side of our sweet-voiced song of triumph hath Righteousness taken her stand

s: Aigina is a island-commonwealth (righteous and glorious)
q: Not far from the Graces' ken falleth the lot of this righteous island-commonwealth

s: Aigina is a nurse of heroes (foremost in many games and violent fights)
q: for she is sung of as the nurse of heroes foremost in many games and in violent fights

s: Aigina is pre eminent mortal men (among her mortal men)
q: and in her mortal men also is she pre-eminent.

s: Aigina belongs to free (as a city in the march among the free)
q: Aigina[9], mother dear, this city in her march among the free

s: Aristomenes follows footsteps of Theognetos (in wrestling)
q: For in wrestlings thou art following the footsteps of thy uncles, and shamest neither Theognetos at Olympia

s: Aigina is protected by Zeus (as its divine guardian)
q: with Zeus and lordly Aiakos, with Peleus and valiant Telamon and with Achilles, guard thou well.

s: Aigina is protected by Aiakos (as its ancestral guardian)
q: with Zeus and lordly Aiakos, with Peleus and valiant Telamon and with Achilles, guard thou well.

s: Aigina is protected by Achilles (as a heroic guardian)
q: with Zeus and lordly Aiakos, with Peleus and valiant Telamon and with Achilles, guard thou well.

s: wrestling-match is won by Aristomenes (at the Pythian games)
q: welcome thou this honour to Aristomenes, won in the Pythian games.

s: Apollo rules temple (the glorious temple at Pytho)
q: But thou, far-darter, ruler of the glorious temple whereto all men go up

s: Apollo welcomes Xenarches (home from Kirrha with Parnassian wreaths and Dorian song)
q: who with kind intent hath welcomed Xenarches home from Kirrha, crowned with Parnassian wreaths and Dorian song.

s: Apollo grants victory (the Pythian prize to Aristomenes)
q: amid the glens of Pytho didst there grant this the greatest of joys

s: Aiakids are descendants of Aiakos (as the heroic descendants of Aiakos)
q: that hath attained unto the glorious deeds of the sons of Aiakos

s: Aristomenes follows footsteps of Kleitomachos (in wrestling)
q: nor the victory that at Isthmos was won by Kleitomachos' stalwart limbs.

s: Aiakos is a ancestor (ancestor of the sons of Aiakos)
q: the glorious deeds of the sons of Aiakos

s: Amphiaraos speaks On this wise
q: On this wise spake Amphiaraos.

s: Amphiaraos foresees Alkmaion (as a speckled dragon on his shield at the Kadmean gates)
q: I see clearly the speckled dragon that Alkmaion weareth on his bright shield, foremost at the Kadmean gates.

s: Amphiaraos foresees Adrastos (as receiving better-omened tidings)
q: And he who in the former fight fared ill, hero Adrastos, is now endowed with tidings of a better omen.

s: Alkmaion wears the speckled dragon (on his bright shield)
q: I see clearly the speckled dragon that Alkmaion weareth on his bright shield

s: Alkmaion protects Pindar's household (as a neighbouring guardian)
q: for that being my neighbour and guardian of my possessions

s: Alkmaion possesses prophecy (as a hereditary gift of his house)
q: and showed forth the gift of prophecy which belongeth unto his house

s: Aristomenes belongs to Midylidai (as a member of the clan)
q: And in that thou makest great the clan of the Midylidai

s: Zeus is associated with Aigina (with Zeus and lordly Aiakos, with Peleus and valiant Telamon and with Achilles)
q: Aigina[9], mother dear, this city in her march among the free, with Zeus and lordly Aiakos, with Peleus and valiant Telamon and with Achilles, guard thou well

s: Achilles is associated with Aigina (with Zeus and lordly Aiakos, with Peleus and valiant Telamon)
q: with Zeus and lordly Aiakos, with Peleus and valiant Telamon and with Achilles

s: Aristomenes wins victory (at Megara)
q: Now at Megara also hast thou won a prize

s: Aristomenes defeats competitors (four competitors in the Pythian wrestling-match)
q: And now on the bodies of four others[8] hast thou hurled thyself with fierce intent

s: Aristomenes is young (in the time of sweet youth)
q: Now he that hath lately won glory in the time of his sweet youth is lifted on the wings of his strong hope and soaring valour

s: Xenarches receives favour the favour of God (unfailing toward the fortune of thee and thine)
q: I pray, O Xenarches[7], that the favour of God be unfailing toward the fortune of thee and thine

s: Xenarches returns home from Kirrha (welcomed by Apollo)
q: who with kind intent hath welcomed Xenarches home from Kirrha, crowned with Parnassian wreaths and Dorian song.

s: Kyrene (the huntress-maiden) is daughter of Hypseus (daughter of the king of the Lapithai)
q: in a common wedlock joined the god and the daughter of wide-ruling Hypseus, who then was king of the haughty Lapithai

s: Kyrene (the huntress-maiden) is a beast-hunter (fighting with bronze javelins and a sword)
q: but with bronze javelins and a sword she fought against and slew wild beasts of prey

s: Kyrene (the huntress-maiden) protects the herds (by killing wild beasts)
q: yea and much peace and sure she gave thereby to her father's herds

s: Apollo is son of Leto (flowing-haired, Delian stranger)
q: Kyrene[1] once from Pelion's wind-echoing dells Leto's son, the flowing-haired, caught up and in a golden car bore away the huntress-maiden

s: Apollo takes as bride Kyrene (the huntress-maiden) (carrying her from Thessaly to Libya)
q: And swift the act and short the ways of gods who are eager to an end. That same day made accomplishment of the matter, and in a golden chamber of Libya they lay together

s: Aphrodite blesses the bridal union of Apollo and Kyrene (at the divine bridal bed)
q: And silver-foot Aphrodite awaited the Delian stranger issuing from his car divine, and lightly laid on him her hand: then over their sweet bridal-bed she cast the loveliness of maiden shame

s: Cheiron is a Centaur (wise and bold)
q: To him the Centaur bold with a frank smile on his mild brow made answer straightway of his wisdom

s: the foot-race in full armour is a race (run in full armour)
q: With a view no doubt to such occasions this race in full armour had been instituted at Pytho in 498

s: Cheiron is son of Philyra
q: Son of Philyra, come forth from thy holy cave

s: Apollo carries the huntress-maiden (in a golden car to the place where he made her queen)
q: Kyrene[1] once from Pelion's wind-echoing dells Leto's son, the flowing-haired, caught up and in a golden car bore away the huntress-maiden to the place where he made her queen of a land rich in flocks

s: Libya gives Kyrene (the huntress-maiden) (a portion of land to inhabit)
q: And now shall queenly Libya of broad meadow-lands well-pleased receive for thee within a golden house thy glorious bride, and there make gift to her of a portion in the land

s: Kyrene is a city (of charioteers)
q: Kyrene, city of charioteers.

s: Kyrene is haunted by she (excellent in beauty and glorious in the games)
q: where now she haunteth a city excellent in beauty and glorious in the games.

s: the foot-race in full armour is held at Pytho
q: With a view no doubt to such occasions this race in full armour had been instituted at Pytho in 498

s: Thebes is a seven-gated city
q: That Iolaos had respect thereto[3] seven-gated Thebes knoweth well

s: Amphitryon is a charioteer
q: the tomb of Amphitryon the charioteer

s: Amphitryon is ancestor of Herakles (father's father according to the passage)
q: where his father's father was laid, a guest of the Spartoi

s: Alkmene is mother of Herakles (with Zeus)
q: To him and to Zeus at once did wise Alkmene bear the strength of twin sons prevailing in battle.

s: Alkmene bears the strength of twin sons (to him and to Zeus at once)
q: To him and to Zeus at once did wise Alkmene bear the strength of twin sons prevailing in battle.

s: Herakles is a hero (whose deeds are continually celebrated)
q: Dull is that man who lendeth not his voice to Herakles

s: Dirke nurtures Herakles (together with Iphikles)
q: nor hath in remembrance continually the waters of Dirke that nurtured him and Iphikles.

s: Telesikrates wins the foot-race in full armour (in 478)
q: and in 478 it was won by Telesikrates.

s: the daughter of Antaios is wooed by the suitors (for love of a Libyan woman)
q: for love of a Libyan woman there went up suitors to the city of Irasa to woo Antaios' lovely-haired daughter of great renown

s: the daughter of Antaios is desired by the suitors (because of her extraordinary beauty)
q: for the beauty of her was marvellous, and they were fain to cull the fruit whereto her gold-crowned youth had bloomed.

s: Danaos organizes the wedding of the Libyan princess (by selecting bridegrooms through a foot-race)
q: Danaos at Argos devised for his forty and eight maiden daughters, ere mid-day was upon them, a wedding of utmost speed--for he straightway set the whole company at the race-course end, and bade determine by a foot-race which maiden each hero should have
